roles.title: AI Operations Analyst
roles.summary: Runs the day-to-day operation of AI systems: monitoring quality, triaging failures, tuning prompts and agents, and keeping a register of what the organisation is actually using.
roles.outlook: Demand is climbing fastest where pilot projects are being turned into production services. Roles are appearing inside operations teams rather than central data labs.

sdgs.rationale: Raises job quality by pairing automation with monitored, human-supervised service delivery.
Builds reliable AI infrastructure inside public and private services.
Creates applied learning pathways for non-specialist staff.
Widens access to AI-era roles beyond computer-science graduates.

roles.title: Data Governance Specialist
roles.summary: Owns the rules, lineage and permissions around data that feeds AI: catalogues datasets, resolves quality disputes and prepares documentation for audits.
roles.outlook: Steady structural demand. Regulation and procurement rules now require named accountability for datasets and model inputs.

sdgs.rationale: Strengthens accountable institutions through traceable, auditable public data.
Enables trustworthy data sharing that underpins decent digital work.
Improves data infrastructure quality across sectors.
Supports interoperable data partnerships between agencies.

roles.title: Green Supply Chain Analyst
roles.summary: Models emissions, materials and supplier risk across a supply chain, then wires the numbers into procurement decisions and disclosure reports.
roles.outlook: Growth follows mandatory climate disclosure and reshoring. The role blends traditional supply-chain analysis with carbon accounting and AI-assisted data collection.

sdgs.rationale: Turns procurement and material flows toward circular, responsible production.
Quantifies and reduces supply-chain emissions.
Protects employment by making local supply chains more competitive.
Upgrades industrial infrastructure with traceable data.
Requires shared supplier reporting standards.

roles.title: Climate Data Steward
roles.summary: Curates climate and environmental datasets — emissions inventories, sensor feeds, adaptation models — so planners can act on evidence rather than vendor dashboards.
roles.outlook: Small but rising occupation. Cities and utilities need people who can judge data quality and translate model uncertainty for decision-makers.

sdgs.rationale: Makes climate action measurable and auditable.
Supplies the evidence base for resilient urban planning.
Improves water and sanitation monitoring data.
Supports land and biodiversity measurement.
Aligns local data with international reporting.

roles.title: AI Product Owner
roles.summary: Decides which AI-enabled services get built, defines acceptable performance and safety thresholds, and holds the line when a demo cannot survive contact with users.
roles.outlook: Demand is strong but concentrated in organisations that already ship software. The differentiator is evaluation discipline, not model access.

sdgs.rationale: Directs AI investment toward productivity that supports decent work.
Turns research capability into dependable public services.
Builds internal capability through delivery.
Sets inclusion requirements at product definition.
Coordinates vendors, agencies and users.

roles.title: Human–AI Interaction Designer
roles.summary: Designs how people delegate to, check and override AI: interfaces, escalation patterns and explanations that hold up under stress.
roles.outlook: Emerging but durable. As agents take more actions, accountability and interface design become procurement requirements.

sdgs.rationale: Keeps AI services usable by people with disabilities and low digital confidence.
Designs human oversight into automated work.
Embeds learning and explanation into tools.
Tests for gendered and other bias in interaction patterns.
Improves access to local public services.

roles.title: Workforce Transition Coach
roles.summary: Guides people displaced or reshaped by automation into adjacent roles: assesses capability, builds a plan and brokers access to training and employers.
roles.outlook: Publicly funded and employer-funded demand is rising together, especially in mid-career transitions where retraining has the highest wage return.

sdgs.rationale: Delivers lifelong learning and recognised reskilling outcomes.
Keeps displaced workers in decent employment.
Prioritises groups furthest from opportunity.
Addresses gendered participation in reskilling.

roles.title: Civic Technology Program Manager
roles.summary: Runs digital and AI programmes in the public interest: procurement, delivery, community engagement and the unglamorous work of making services usable.
roles.outlook: Stable demand tied to digital public infrastructure budgets. AI procurement scrutiny is increasing the value of experienced programme leaders.

sdgs.rationale: Delivers better local services and inclusive urban systems.
Makes public technology accountable and transparent.
Brokers partnerships across sectors and levels of government.
Builds reusable public digital infrastructure.
Designs services for those least able to navigate them.

roles.title: Cyber Resilience Analyst
roles.summary: Protects services that now depend on models and APIs: threat models AI pipelines, hardens identity and detects abuse of automated systems.
roles.outlook: Very strong demand. AI adoption expands the attack surface, and security teams are hiring for AI-specific assurance rather than classic perimeter work.

sdgs.rationale: Protects public institutions and citizens from digital harm.
Keeps critical digital infrastructure resilient.
Safeguards business continuity and jobs.
Requires threat information sharing.

roles.title: AI Ethics & Compliance Officer
roles.summary: Turns principles into controls: impact assessments, bias testing, vendor terms and incident processes that survive the first serious complaint.
roles.outlook: Growing from a low base. Regulation, procurement and reputational risk are converting voluntary frameworks into named responsibilities.

sdgs.rationale: Builds accountable institutions for automated decision-making.
Tests and mitigates discriminatory outcomes.
Raises organisational AI literacy and transparency.
Audits gendered impact of automated systems.
Aligns practice with international standards.

roles.title: Energy Systems Data Analyst
roles.summary: Models demand, generation and grid constraints, increasingly including the electricity appetite of data centres and electrified transport.
roles.outlook: Rising demand driven by electrification and AI infrastructure. Utilities are hiring analysts who can work with both market data and engineering constraints.

sdgs.rationale: Improves energy access, efficiency and clean generation planning.
Supports decarbonisation of power systems.
Strengthens resilient energy infrastructure.
Informs sustainable city energy planning.
Depends on regional grid cooperation.

roles.title: Healthcare Automation Specialist
roles.summary: Automates scheduling, documentation and triage support in care settings while keeping clinicians accountable and patients safe.
roles.outlook: Rising but regulated. Adoption is fastest in administrative workflows, slower where clinical risk is high.

sdgs.rationale: Frees clinical time and reduces administrative harm.
Reshapes care work rather than simply removing it.
Modernises health information infrastructure.
Extends access where clinical capacity is scarce.

scenarios.name: Baseline Adoption 2028
scenarios.summary: Enterprises keep adopting AI at the current pace. Task-level automation spreads unevenly, reskilling demand grows steadily and policy remains mostly facilitative.
assumptions: Enterprise AI adoption continues along its 2024–2026 trend
Regulation is implemented without major new obligations
Public reskilling budgets grow modestly with inflation

drivers.name: Task-level automation
drivers.detail: Clerical and first-line support tasks are partially automated; roles are reshaped rather than removed.

drivers.name: Evaluation maturity
drivers.detail: Buyers start requiring evidence of model quality and incident handling.

drivers.name: Skills shortages
drivers.detail: AI operations and governance talent remains the binding constraint.

scenarios.name: Accelerated Automation 2028
scenarios.summary: Agentic systems move from assistant to actor. Task displacement accelerates in mid-skill work, while demand spikes for people who can supervise, evaluate and repair automated operations.
assumptions: Agent reliability improves enough for multi-step production use
Cost per automated task falls 60% below 2026 levels
Firms restructure teams around AI operations rather than adding tools

drivers.name: Agentic deployment
drivers.detail: Multi-step agents take over workflows in service operations, finance and back-office.

drivers.name: Evaluation gap
drivers.detail: Failures in production increase demand for AI operations and assurance roles.

drivers.name: Entry-level compression
drivers.detail: Junior analytical and administrative roles shrink, worsening transitions for new graduates.

assumptions: Mandatory climate disclosure covers most listed firms and their suppliers
AI assurance requirements are enforced with named accountability
Public procurement favours demonstrably safe and inclusive systems

drivers.name: Climate disclosure

drivers.name: Public trust

green-supply-chain-analyst.note: Disclosure rules reach deep into supplier networks.
